title: Drone Threats Force Cities to Rethink Defenses
summary: As drones become cheaper, faster and harder to detect, cities far from traditional battlefields are confronting the challenge of protecting civilians without creating new risks from falling debris or costly interceptions. Bloomberg Weekend Senior Writer Morgan Meaker is on Bloomberg This Weekend and examines how governments are testing everything from jammers and interceptor drones to surprisingly effective low tech nets as they search for defenses that can keep pace with rapidly evolving threats. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Shelton Eyes End to US Men’s Grand Slam Drought
summary: Ben Shelton heads into the US Open final with a chance to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam singles title since Andy Roddick in 2003, potentially giving US men’s tennis a new marquee star. Bloomberg News Business of Sports Reporter Vanessa Perdomo joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss Shelton and also broader questions across sports ranging from college eligibility rules to the NFL’s push into international markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How Will Silicon Valley Rearm America?
summary: War in Ukraine, conflict in the Middle East and the rise of China have pushed national security back to the center of US economic and industrial strategy. Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper says the country needs to spend more on defense and better use cutting-edge weapons coming out of places like Silicon Valley, Austin and Boston. The opportunity is particularly striking in space, where companies like Apex Space are trying to industrialize satellite production as the US considers ambitious projects like Golden Dome . But the new defense-tech boom still faces hard questions: will the Pentagon procure quickly enough; will startups scale production;  is space-based missile defense technically and financially realistic; and will the future belong to startups, legacy primes, or a marriage between the two? (Source: Bloomberg)

title: LIV Golf’s $5 Billion Path to Bankruptcy
summary: LIV shook professional golf with flashy tournaments and big payouts, thanks to billions of dollars in backing from the Saudi sovereign wealth fund. On today’s Big Take podcast, David Gura and Golf.com senior writer Sean Zak look at why LIV Golf couldn’t make the cut — and how it changed pro golf. Listen wherever you get your podcasts.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Traders Hedging Stock Rally Split on Plunge or Drift Protection
summary: Investors looking to hedge as the equity rally stalls in the face of rising interest rates and oil prices are split between protecting against a fast selloff or a slow grind lower.

title: Trump Urges Zelenskyy to Stop Hitting Russia’s Diesel Refineries
summary: President Donald Trump says Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has to stop striking Russia’s diesel fuel refineries because it’s “hurting the world.”

title: Wall Street Says Stay With Stocks Despite Late ‘90s Dot-Com Vibe
summary: Rising bond yields and soaring oil prices have many Wall Street pros looking back a few decades to the volatile period before the dot-com crash. But that doesn’t mean they’re encouraging investors to dump their stocks.

title: After Oil Surge and War, Emerging Markets Unfazed by Fed Risk
summary: Emerging markets have defied war, $100 oil and rising Treasury yields this year. And despite worries of a US interest-rate hike, investors see reasons for this year’s rally to keep going.

title: Therapists Explore a Hybrid Future With AI
summary: Therapists are experimenting with AI twins that can mimic how they communicate, giving patients greater access while allowing practitioners to scale their time. Journalist and Bloomberg Features Writer Isabel Woodford joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and examines the potential benefits alongside concerns about safety, liability and whether increasingly capable AI could reshape the economics and intimacy of therapy. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Iran Seeks Gulf Support for Hormuz Plan
summary: Gulf states are weighing how to respond to Iran’s push for a new arrangement governing the Strait of Hormuz as continued attacks threaten shipping and drive up energy costs. On Bloomberg This Weekend,  Bloomberg News Middle East Reporter Dan Williams and Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Skylar Woodhouse discuss growing regional frustration with the conflict, pressure on US allies and signs Gulf governments may be looking for a larger role in shaping a path forward. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Pacific Island Bougainville Vows Action After Alleged Mine Arson
summary: The Autonomous Bougainville Government vowed to take action after alleged arson destroyed equipment at a giant Papua New Guinea copper mine that recently began efforts to restart almost 40 years after it was shut down.

title: Can Scotland’s Abundant Wind Power a Data Center Boom?
summary: Scotland produces far more wind power than its grid can handle, forcing turbines to be shut down when supply exceeds demand or transmission capacity. Developers now see a possible solution: build data centers close to the surplus power, turning wasted wind into compute capacity for AI and the digital economy.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ukraine Says Passenger Train Headed to Warsaw Hit by Drone
summary: The locomotive of a passenger train traveling from Kyiv to Warsaw was hit by a Russian drone just kilometers from the Polish border on Sunday morning, Ukraine’s foreign minister said, as Moscow’s airstrikes push closer to NATO territory.

title: Senegal Raises $179 Million as Debt Rework Tests Local Market
summary: Senegal raised 101 billion CFA francs ($179 million) in a government securities auction on Friday, its first sale since announcing plans to seek a reworking of its external debt.

summary: The 18th BRICS summit hosted in New Delhi comes to a wrap. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: RBI Said to Reject Tata Sons Request to Avoid An IPO
summary: India’s central bank rejected an application from Tata Sons Pvt. to surrender its status as a shadow lender, according to people familiar with the matter, signaling it expects the company to adhere with rules for such entities that include an initial public offering.

title: Korea Tests Global Investor Appetite With Longer Trading Hours
summary: South Korea’s main stock exchange is extending into evening sessions, breaking with Asia’s trading-hour norms to tap what it hopes will be sustained demand from global investors.

title: SpaceX to Get Weighting Boost in Nasdaq 100 After Rebalance
summary: SpaceX is set to get a larger weighting in the Nasdaq 100 later this month, a change that could trigger billions of dollars of buying by passive funds tied to the benchmark.
